page: Amazon Web Services c8id.32xlarge is a compute-optimized server powered by an Intel Xeon 6975P-C processor with x86_64 architecture. It features 128 vCPUs across 64 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled, operating at a clock speed of 3.9 GHz. The processor includes a 480 MB L3 cache and supports Advanced Vector Extensions (AVX-512) and Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX). The system is equipped with 256.0 GB of DDR5 memory running at 7 GHz, providing 2.0 GB of memory per core. It also includes 7600 GB of local NVMe SSD instance storage and a baseline network bandwidth of 50 Gbps, managed via the Nitro hypervisor.

In benchmark evaluations, the c8id.32xlarge demonstrates top-tier multi-core processing capabilities, placing in the top 10% for stress-ng multi-core CPU performance, PassMark CPU score, and Geekbench multi-core score. Single-core performance is more moderate, with stress-ng single-core CPU performance falling into the middle 50%. Memory bandwidth is highly efficient, with read-only small block and large block operations both ranking in the top 10%. The server also excels in database operations, achieving top-tier results in PassMark database tests and Redis SET operations, which reached 211.81 million operations per second.

The server's hardware profile presents a specific resource density tradeoff, offering high compute power and fast DDR5 memory bandwidth but a relatively low memory-to-vCPU ratio of 2 GB per core. This makes it highly cost-efficient for compute-bound workloads that do not require massive RAM footprints, but less suitable for memory-intensive in-memory databases. The inclusion of 7600 GB of local NVMe SSD storage provides high-speed local scratch space, reducing the need for external block storage. Appropriate workloads include multi-threaded data decompression, static web serving, software compilation, and CPU-based LLM prompt processing, where its AMX instructions and top-tier multi-core throughput can be fully utilized.
